# Commands

Inspect the window with `herdr-app ls` and `herdr-app status`.
`herdr-app commands` lists the app actions below, even without an open window.

Run an action in the open window with `herdr-app do`:

```sh
herdr-app do pane.split --direction right
herdr-app do pane.split '{"direction":"right"}'
```

Arguments can be named flags or one JSON object. Required arguments are marked below.
Actions use the current selection unless you give an explicit target.
Some actions close terminals; read their descriptions before running them.
Mods can add their own actions, which are not listed here.

## `space.new`

Make a space: its name (default: none, so it's called after where its first terminal is), the folder its terminals start in (default: the focused terminal's; empty string: the home folder of the machine the space lives on, this computer's or another machine's), its first tab's name (default: none, so it's called by its number), optionally an agent (argv) and its first message (task), and the machine it lives on (`hc machine ls`; default the focused space's machine for keys and clicks, this computer for scripts; empty string: this computer; its terminals start in that machine's home unless folder). It is shown at once; focus false keeps the shown space and tab (with no space shown, the new space is shown).

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `name` | no |
| `folder` | no |
| `tab` | no |
| `argv` | no |
| `task` | no |
| `machine` | no |
| `focus` | no |

## `space.close`

Close a space and end its terminals (asks first unless confirmed).

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `id` | no |
| `confirmed` | no |

## `space.rename`

Rename a space (asks the person when no name; an empty name: called after where its first terminal is again).

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `id` | no |
| `name` | no |

## `space.move`

Move a space to a position (1 = first).

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `id` | yes |
| `index` | yes |

## `tab.new`

Make a tab in a space (default: the selected one; name default: none, so it's called by its number) with a terminal in folder (default: the focused terminal's; empty string: the space's machine's home), optionally an agent (argv) and its first message (task); or with a mod as its only pane (`mod`, its `props`: a file, a board). It is shown at once; focus false adds it last in its space (a tab opened for an agent: after that agent's tabs) and keeps the shown space and the target space's selected tab. With no space open, a person's new tab starts a space (as space.new).

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `name` | no |
| `space` | no |
| `folder` | no |
| `argv` | no |
| `task` | no |
| `mod` | no |
| `props` | no |
| `focus` | no |

## `tab.close`

Close a tab and end its terminals.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `id` | no |
| `confirmed` | no |

## `tab.rename`

Rename a tab (asks the person when no name; an empty name: called by its number again).

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `id` | no |
| `name` | no |

## `tab.move`

Move a tab (the active one if no id) to a position in its space (1 = first), or `by` places left (-) or right (+), wrapping.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `id` | no |
| `index` | no |
| `by` | no |

## `pane.split`

Split a pane (default: the focused one) "right" or "down" with a new terminal in folder (default: the pane's terminal's folder; empty string: the pane's machine's home), or with a mod (`mod`, its `props`) beside it.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `direction` | yes |
| `pane` | no |
| `argv` | no |
| `folder` | no |
| `mod` | no |
| `props` | no |

## `pane.close`

Close a pane and end its terminal.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `pane` | no |

## `app.open`

Open a mod as an app in a tab of its own (title: its name; default: the app's label) and show it. It is opened for the agent the pane of `for` works for (a terminal: an address, or the id on its machine with space naming its space there; default: the focused pane): that agent's own terminal, else the agent the pane's tab was opened for, else the agent focused last in that tab. Its tab goes after the agent's tab and its earlier tabs and closes with the agent; without an agent it goes after the selected tab. app: which of the mod's mod.json `app` registrations it is. props get `app` (the registration), `origin` (the agent) and `project` (the agent's Git work tree or folder) unless given. An open app is shown again instead, its running copy given the props from nextLink(): with reuse "agent" (the default, or the registration's `reuse`) the one opened for that agent, "project" the one for that agent on the same project, "none" never, and no later open shows one opened so (its props get `reuse: "none"`). Returns space, tab, pane and reused.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `mod` | yes |
| `app` | no |
| `props` | no |
| `title` | no |
| `for` | no |
| `space` | no |
| `reuse` | no |

## `app.beside`

Move an app's tab (default: the selected one) into the tab of the agent it was opened for, right of the agent's pane. The app keeps running.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `tab` | no |

## `app.apart`

Move an app beside its agent (default: the focused pane) back into a tab of its own after the agent's tab. The app keeps running.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `pane` | no |

## `terminal.open`

Start a terminal: as a new tab (place "tab", default), or "right"/"down" of the focused pane.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `argv` | no |
| `folder` | no |
| `place` | no |
| `name` | no |

## `terminal.keep`

Give a running terminal without a pane (a sub-agent) a pane: a new tab, or "right"/"down".

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `terminal` | yes |
| `place` | no |

## `terminal.park`

Take a terminal's pane away and disable core keep; it keeps running (a sub-agent shows under its parent again).

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `terminal` | yes |

## `terminal.right_click`

Where right-clicks in a terminal (default: the focused one) go when its program takes the mouse: "program" or "menu" (Herdr's, the default). Shift+right-click is always the menu.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `to` | yes |
| `terminal` | no |

## `terminal.pin`

Pin an agent to the top of the agent lists (pinned true) or unpin it (false). Pins are kept with the terminal, so every Herdr client shows them, and end with it.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `terminal` | yes |
| `pinned` | yes |

## `terminal.kill`

End a terminal and its sub-agents. Spare branches whose first sub-agent has a pane or a herdr.space label. Core still applies parent-lifetime rules.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `terminal` | yes |

## `pane.view`

Show a pane's GUI or terminal view: view is "gui", "tui" or "toggle". Target a pane or terminal; default: the focused pane. The choice is kept in the terminal label herdr.view; an unavailable GUI falls back to the terminal.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `view` | yes |
| `pane` | no |
| `terminal` | no |

## `pane.go`

Focus the pane or focusable mod to the "left", "right", "up" or "down".

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `direction` | yes |

## `pane.resize`

Move the border of a pane (default: the focused one) "left", "right", "up" or "down" by px (default 40), like dragging the divider.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `direction` | yes |
| `pane` | no |
| `px` | no |

## `pane.header_height`

Give a pane's header (default: the focused pane's) the height px, from the pane header mod that draws in it, so a footer can grow with its content. The layout's header height is the least it gets and its max_height (default 400) the most; px null or missing takes the request back. The request is kept for this running app, not saved, and ends with the header mod's copy (a layout switch, a mod reload, a closed pane). Returns {px}: the height the header now has.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `pane` | no |
| `px` | no |

## `pane.swap`

Swap a pane (default: the focused one) with its neighbor in a direction, or with another pane of its tab (target). Give exactly one of direction or target.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `direction` | no |
| `pane` | no |
| `target` | no |

## `terminal.peek`

Peek at a running terminal over the tab, with keep-as-tab and close controls.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `terminal` | yes |

## `terminal.show`

Show a terminal in a pane for now, in place of its own (no terminal: back).

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `terminal` | no |
| `pane` | no |

## `terminal.select_all`

Select a terminal's whole screen and scrollback (default: the focused one), ready to copy. On the alternate screen, select only that screen.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `terminal` | no |

## `terminal.select`

Start a terminal selection (default: the focused one), replacing the old selection. at defaults to "cursor" or takes {row, col}: zero-based cells, rows from the top of the history including the active screen. mode is "cell" (default), "word" or "line" (like double/triple click). With to: {row, col}, the endpoints are exact and the view follows to. Line mode with to selects whole screen rows. Mods read the inclusive endpoints from focused().selection or terminals(); selection.end is the moving end.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `terminal` | no |
| `at` | no |
| `to` | no |
| `mode` | no |

## `terminal.adjust_selection`

Move the selection's moving end: left, right, up, down, page_up, page_down, home, end, line_start or line_end. The view follows the moving end. Fails if there is no selection. Defaults to the focused terminal.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `terminal` | no |
| `direction` | yes |

## `terminal.clear_selection`

Clear a terminal's selection (default: the focused one).

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `terminal` | no |

## `terminal.copy`

Copy the focused terminal's selection. With nothing selected, that key goes to the program.

No arguments.

## `terminal.scroll`

Scroll a terminal's view of its history (default: the focused one). Give exactly one of: lines (a whole number; negative goes up, toward history), pages (a number, fractions allowed; one page is the terminal's rows), to: "top" (oldest history) or "bottom" (the live screen). This scrolls Herdr's view, not the program.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `lines` | no |
| `pages` | no |
| `to` | no |
| `terminal` | no |

## `terminal.send_key`

Send one key in keys.json syntax, such as ctrl-b, to a terminal (default: the focused one). It uses the program's current keyboard mode and goes through the same connection as typing. The terminal must have a view.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `keys` | yes |
| `terminal` | no |

## `terminal.paste`

Paste into the focused terminal (copied files as if dropped; an image alone as terminal.paste_image pastes it).

No arguments.

## `terminal.paste_image`

Ctrl+V: the clipboard's image as a file on the focused terminal's machine, when that's another one; on Windows, paste clipboard text; otherwise Ctrl+V goes to the terminal.

No arguments.

## `terminal.search`

Search the focused terminal's screen and scrollback; the find bar and query stay with that terminal.

No arguments.

## `link.open`

Open a link as clicking it in a terminal does: a URL, or a file or folder path (`:42` or `:42:7` after it names a line and column) on the terminal's machine, relative to cwd (default: the terminal's folder). terminal: the terminal it came from (an address, or the id on its machine with space naming its space there); tabs opened for an agent's link belong to that agent. A mod waiting in nextLink() shows it in a tab; otherwise, or with system true, the system's program opens it.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `target` | yes |
| `terminal` | no |
| `space` | no |
| `cwd` | no |
| `system` | no |

## `agent.list`

List Pi agents in the running app, optionally in an exact space or on one machine (empty string: this computer). Returns stable terminal, space and tab ids, current PID and Pi session, and startup state.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `space` | no |
| `machine` | no |

## `agent.inspect`

Inspect an exact terminal address: Pi timeline, current identity, question and error. Set screen true for the full terminal screen and 0–400 history lines (default 80), or false for metadata only. An unavailable Pi returns an error; reload its integration.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `terminal` | yes |
| `lines` | no |
| `screen` | no |

## `agent.history`

Read the current Pi session branch. Page before an exclusive item index (default end), limit 1–50 (default 20). Query searches literal text, at most 200 characters, newest matches first; caseSensitive defaults to false.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `terminal` | yes |
| `query` | no |
| `caseSensitive` | no |
| `before` | no |
| `limit` | no |

## `agent.send`

Send a message to the inspected Pi agent. Rejects changed identities, agents still starting, and blocked user questions; never forces input.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `terminal` | yes |
| `pid` | yes |
| `session` | yes |
| `message` | yes |

## `agent.stop`

Interrupt the inspected Pi agent with its stop key. Does not kill it or escalate; returns the observed outcome.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `terminal` | yes |
| `pid` | yes |
| `session` | yes |

## `agent.remove`

End the inspected Pi agent and remove its dedicated single-pane tab. Rejects changed identities and tabs with sibling panes.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `terminal` | yes |
| `pid` | yes |
| `session` | yes |

## `workflow.get`

Read the persisted workflow profiles: each one's id, name, description of when to use it, primary model, startup-only fallback model, and thinking level.

No arguments.

## `workflow.set`

Update one workflow profile atomically; omitted fields stay. Models use provider/model ids; pass fallbackModel null to disable it. The name stays non-empty; description "" or null clears it. Existing agents keep their model.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `profile` | yes |
| `model` | no |
| `fallbackModel` | no |
| `thinking` | no |
| `name` | no |
| `description` | no |

## `workflow.add`

Add a workflow profile. Its id is unique lowercase kebab-case, such as review or quick-fix; thinking defaults to high. Returns all profiles.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `id` | yes |
| `name` | yes |
| `model` | yes |
| `description` | no |
| `fallbackModel` | no |
| `thinking` | no |

## `workflow.remove`

Remove a workflow profile; the last one can go too. Running agents keep their model. Returns the remaining profiles.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `profile` | yes |

## `workflow.models`

Read Pi's configured model scope on one machine without a running Pi (default: the selected space's; empty string: this computer). Returns a cached snapshot with loading, diagnostics and errors, supplemented by current live Pi catalogs, plus extension installation status. Model selection does not prove launch availability.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `machine` | no |
